s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of systemic illness with fever, weakness, abdominal pain, and bleeding, accompanied by hepatosplenomegaly and pancytopenia
salient_findings: Pancytopenia with abnormal blastoid cells on peripheral smear
Hepatosplenomegaly with splenic infarction
Bilateral subdural hemorrhages and pleural effusions
Extensive pulmonary consolidation and thrombosis of the celiac artery
Bone marrow aspirate showing trilineage dysplasia and immature metachromatic blasts
key_facts: 39-year-old man with a history of treated tuberculosis
Two weeks of fever, generalized weakness, and vague abdominal pain
Moderate nasal bleeding
2×1 cm submandibular lymph node
Hepatomegaly (7 cm below the costal margin)
Urea 18.8 mmol/L, creatinine 141 µmol/L
Lipase 182 U/L, myoglobin 108 ng/mL, ferritin >40 000 µg/L
Vitamin B12 <111 pmol/L
Normal fibrinogen and triglycerides
Viral serologies were negative
Pancytopenia: hemoglobin 6.4 g/dL, WBC 1.7×10^3/µL, ANC 0.9×10^3/µL, platelets 2×10^3/µL
Bone marrow aspirate was hypercellular with 26% immature metachromatic blasts
Trilineage dysplasia with megaloblastic changes in granulocytes and erythroid precursors

shortlist.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of 26% immature metachromatic blasts in bone marrow aspirate and 13% abnormal blastoid cells in peripheral smear

shortlist.label: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Trilineage dysplasia with megaloblastic changes in granulocytes and erythroid precursors, and presence of pancytopenia

shortlist.label: Myeloproliferative Neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Hepatosplenomegaly and presence of immature metachromatic blasts in bone marrow aspirate

shortlist.label: Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of immature metachromatic blasts in bone marrow aspirate and monocytosis is not explicitly ruled out

shortlist.label: Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of abnormal blastoid cells in peripheral smear and bone marrow aspirate with coarse granules and bilobed nuclei

raw.rationale: The presence of 26% immature metachromatic blasts in the bone marrow aspirate and 13% abnormal blastoid cells in the peripheral smear, along with trilineage dysplasia and megaloblastic changes, strongly supports the diagnosis of Acute Myeloid Leukemia.

rejected.label: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
rejected.why: While trilineage dysplasia is present, the high percentage of blasts in the bone marrow is more indicative of Acute Myeloid Leukemia than Myelodysplastic Syndrome.

rejected.label: Myeloproliferative Neoplasm
rejected.why: The presence of pancytopenia and lack of significant proliferation in any lineage argues against Myeloproliferative Neoplasm.

rejected.label: Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia
rejected.why: The high blast percentage and acute presentation are not typical of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia.

rejected.label: Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm
rejected.why: The morphology of the blasts and the presence of trilineage dysplasia do not support Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm.
